findings: The raw repository source preserves only the interview prompt '算法：大数相乘'; the candidate does not import a hidden online-judge contract and labels decimal nonnegative string semantics as an explicit candidate API choice.

The candidate directly explains the grade-school multiplication invariant: each digit-pair contribution is accumulated at the corresponding decimal weight, then right-to-left carry normalization preserves the represented numeric value.

The implementation and prose agree on null, empty, non-digit, leading-zero and canonical-zero behavior; the earlier unsupported claim that whitespace had an explicit fixed test was removed before this review.
The recorded Java fixture passes 14 fixed checks and 4000 deterministic randomized pairs against an independent BigInteger oracle, and checks commutativity for every randomized pair.
The O(m*n) time and O(m+n) auxiliary-space claims match the implementation structure and no production or personal experience is fabricated.
